run.rulesInOwnWords:
State: six positions (1 = source end, 6 = load end). Each position has a quantity (a whole number, never negative), a cap (rated charge), an upper mark, a lower mark, and a two-value state (ASSERTED or CLEAR). All six start CLEAR, and the loss tally starts at 0. Each cycle runs Steps 1 to 5 in order, and each step is finished for all six positions before the next step starts.
Step 1 (input): add that cycle's row of the input table to each position. The cap is not applied here.
Step 2 (overflow, sequential 1 to 6): if a position holds more than its cap, move the excess into position n+1 and set the position to its cap. Excess from position 6 goes to loss. Because the pass runs in order, overflow that arrives at a position counts when that position is checked, so one overflow can set off the next all the way down the chain.
Step 3 (hysteresis state): a CLEAR position becomes ASSERTED if its quantity is at or above its upper mark. An ASSERTED position becomes CLEAR if its quantity is at or below its lower mark. Otherwise the state does not change. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, before, after).
Step 4 (simultaneous discharge): work out every amount from the post-Step-2 quantities. A CLEAR position discharges floor(q/4) and an ASSERTED position discharges floor(q/2). Then apply all six together. Each position loses its own amount. A CLEAR amount goes to loss. An ASSERTED amount is added to position n-1, except that position 1's ASSERTED amount goes to loss. The cap is not applied, so overflow carries into the next cycle's Step 2, or into the end figures if this is cycle 5.
Step 5 (global reset): if the six quantities sum to strictly more than 38, every position is halved and rounded down, the removed amount goes to loss, and the cycle is logged. A sum of exactly 38 does not trip.

run.balanceCheck: Starting charges: 3+6+6+2+2+1 = 20. All thirty inputs: 20+14+17+24+18 = 94. Left side: 20 + 94 = 114. End charges: 6+10+9+7+4+2 = 38. Ground total: 76. Right side: 38 + 76 = 114. The two sides are equal (114 = 114).
run.notes: I used a short Python script for the arithmetic (scratchpad sim.py) and checked every cycle again by hand; the results agree. Edge cases handled as written: (1) In cycle 5 the end sum is exactly 38, so there is no trip, because the rule is strictly greater than 38. (2) Return-diode feedback can push a stage over its rated charge, and stages 2 (10 > 8) and 4 (7 > 6) stay over-rated in the end figures, as the document says. (3) Stage 1's ASSERTED discharge goes to ground. (4) In cycle 4 the breakdown shunt cascades through all six stages. (5) Every comparator decision uses the post-Step-2 charge.
run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror, FILTER MODE (default).
Step 1, plain statement: six ordered integer counters with caps and two thresholds each, plus a two-state flag per counter. Each cycle does five things in order: add the inputs; run one sequential overflow pass from 1 to 6 that pushes excess forward, with position 6's excess lost; update each flag with hysteresis (set at or above the upper mark, cleared at or below the lower mark, otherwise held); discharge all counters at the same moment, using floor(q/4) if the flag is clear (lost) or floor(q/2) if the flag is set (passed back one position, and lost at position 1); and halve everything if the total is more than 38, with the removed amount lost. The quantities are conserved: start plus inputs equals end plus lost. The document's electrical framing is the embedded comparison and becomes picture 1. The plain statement is enough to run the job, but the pre-read asks for the pictures, so they are tested below.
Step 2, pictures: (P1) the document's own electrical picture, a charge chain with a breakdown shunt, a Schmitt trigger, a return diode, ground and a breaker; (P2) a cascade of water tanks with overflow weirs; (P3) a ledger with transfers and write-offs.
Steps 3 and 4, map and break: P1 maps a stage to a capacitor, the shunt to forward overflow, the Schmitt trigger to the hysteresis flag, ground to loss, and the breaker to the global halving. Where it breaks: a real diode conducts toward lower potential, not always toward n-1. A real breaker opens the circuit; it does not halve charge. Real discharge is continuous, not floor(q/4). Real overvoltage would not persist past the shunt step. Reading P1 literally would import real physics that contradicts the stated rules. It can only mislead if used in place of the rules, and it does not contradict them when used as a label set, so it is graded below. P2 maps a tank to a stage and a weir to the cap. Where it breaks: tanks spill continuously and all at once, not in a single 1-to-6 ordered pass, and backflow uphill to n-1 is not a natural tank behavior. Its one useful question: does order matter in the overflow pass? Yes, and the document already says so explicitly. P3 maps the quantities to account balances and loss to written-off amounts. It does not break; conservation holds exactly.
Step 5, what survives: P1, the flag depends on its own previous state, which the document already states. P2, the overflow pass is sequential and can cascade, which the document already states. P3, the total is conserved, so start plus inputs equals end plus loss, which the document's balance check already states.
Step 6, grading: all three restate what the document already says explicitly. Adds nothing: 3 of 3. Misleading: 0. Not run: 0. (P1 would become misleading if real electrical behavior were substituted for the written rules, for example letting a diode block the n-1 feedback, or treating the breaker as zeroing the chain. The desk note forbids this, so I note it here rather than discard the picture.)
Step 7, piles: Keep exploring: empty. Hold: empty. Discard: empty. No instructions aimed at the reader were found inside the operating document. The operating rules were applied exactly as written.
